drhp.business: Caliber is a mining operator that manages overburden removal, coal extraction and coal logistics together as an integrated services provider, offering end-to-end services including coal extraction, overburden removal, coal loading/unloading, road transportation and rail coordination. It provides contractual coal extraction and overburden removal at open cast mines it does not own, primarily for Coal India subsidiaries WCL and NCL, and runs a logistics business for coal and iron ore. Operations are located in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
drhp.end_markets: Coal mining services (86.08% of FY26 revenue from operations)|Logistics (12.44% of FY26 revenue from operations)|Coal trading (0.92% of FY26 revenue from operations)|Rake loading (0.54% of FY26 revenue from operations)|Rail coordination services (0.02% of FY26 revenue from operations)
drhp.expansion: Caliber has been expanding capacity through large investment in vehicles, plant and machinery, increasing overburden removal by 88.18% from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026. As of April 30, 2026 it owned 1,811 and leased 100 vehicles, plant and machinery (including 883 mining tippers, 362 tip trailers, 162 excavators, 64 loaders, 65 bulldozers and 32 graders). Net proceeds of the Offer are proposed to fund further capital expenditure for the purchase of commercial vehicles, plant and machinery.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Integrated end-to-end coal mining and logistics services provider offering coal extraction, overburden removal, coal loading and unloading, road transportation and coordination of rail transportation as a one-stop provider. Owns its fleet (1,811 owned and 100 leased vehicles, plant and machinery as of April 30, 2026), enabling cost, scheduling and customer-service advantages over leased fleets. Conducts in-house and preventive maintenance at its own workshops (headquarters at Chandrapur plus seven mining sites), providing cost savings. Procures high-speed diesel a month in advance directly from local refineries at favourable rates to reduce diesel expenses and short-term price exposure. Maximises economies of scale through integration of mining and logistics services, and uses ERP across operations, procurement, dispatch and accounting.

internal_operational.detail: Company is not the owner of the mines; it extracts coal and removes overburden under mining contracts. Open cast operations exposed to mining accidents, injuries/fatalities, health and safety shutdowns, pit flooding, slope failure, truck/machinery/equipment failures, and interruptions in diesel and water supply. Diesel is a significant portion of operating cost and its price is exposed to the ongoing US/Iran/Israel energy crisis; current mining contract has diesel escalation/de-escalation clause but increases not covered could hurt margins.
internal_operational.evidence: In Fiscal 2026 consumed 85,226.77 kilolitres of high-speed diesel. Power and fuel expense: FY2026 78,391.48 lakhs (53.51% of total expenses), FY2025 67,289.14 lakhs (53.47%), FY2024 42,744.35 lakhs (51.53%). Monthly average diesel fuel expense FY2026 6,532.62 lakhs, FY2025 5,607.43 lakhs, FY2024 3,562.03 lakhs. No material incidents in FY2026/FY2025/FY2024.

strategy_growth.detail: Large-scale mining contracts (over 100,000 lakhs, 2-3 year terms) represented a majority of revenue and Order Book; award of future contracts is unpredictable, subject to competitive bidding, pre-qualifications and performance security; cancellations/scope changes may occur.
strategy_growth.evidence: Contracts over 100,000 lakhs 1,27,695.52 lakhs (76.12% of revenue) FY2026, 91,188.02 (63.75%) FY2025, 25,735.63 (27.00%) FY2024. Coal mining services represented 5,28,691.89 lakhs (93.27% of Order Book) as of March 31, 2026. Order book 9,55,089.08 lakhs as at May 15, 2026.
strategy_growth.title: Dependence on large-scale mining contracts (over 100,000 lakhs) and uncertainty of winning future awards

strategy_growth.detail: Strategy to expand into new geographies; no outstanding tender applications yet; expansion subjects the company to unfamiliar cultural/economic conditions, staffing difficulties and new competitors.
strategy_growth.evidence: No outstanding application to participate in tenders in Odisha and Jharkhand as of the RHP date.
strategy_growth.title: May not succeed in expansion into Odisha and Jharkhand

strategy_growth.detail: Competes with regional and national companies for mining contracts (primarily from CIL and subsidiaries) and with organized/unorganized logistics providers; peers may have better margins, scale and financial resources.
strategy_growth.evidence: Listed peers: Power Mech Projects, NCC Limited, Sindhu Trade Links, Dilip Buildcon. Caliber PAT margin FY2026 9.41%; Operating EBITDA margin 25.69%; Net Debt/Equity 1.62x (higher than several peers).
strategy_growth.title: Competitive industry; peers may be larger with better margins and financial ratios

concerns_observed: Extreme customer concentration: top 3 customers = 90.11% of FY26 revenue, single largest (NCL) 44.16%; top 10 = 98.40%. Standard-form WCL/NCL contracts favour the counterparty (no liability cap in some, customer termination and tender-barring rights, latent site-defect risk with no recourse).

Asset-light on the underlying resource: the Company owns no mines or coal reserves and depends on winning/renewing 2-3 year contracts; contracts over Rs 1,000 cr each contributed 76.12% of FY26 revenue.

High leverage: aggregate borrowings Rs 1,057.61 cr at March 31, 2026 (D/E 1.63x; 1.33x FY25, 2.45x FY24), DSCR a thin 1.12x, finance cost Rs 81.25 cr; Rs 208 cr of Net Proceeds is earmarked to repay borrowings.

Diesel-dependent, fixed-rate margin exposure: power and fuel was 53.51% of total expenses (Rs 783.91 cr) in FY26; mining is mostly on fixed rates with only partial escalation cover, and diesel is exposed to global energy prices.
Contingent liabilities of Rs 458.53 cr = 70.81% of net worth at FY26 (up from 28.51% FY25), predominantly bank guarantees of Rs 440.14 cr.

Heavy related-party dependence: sale of services to related parties was Rs 271.84 cr (16.35% of FY26 revenue), including KSR Freight Carriers - a partnership of all Promoters that is simultaneously a top-3 customer (5.00% of revenue); logistics services are taken from Shree Chadda Roadlines, for which the Company also gave a corporate guarantee.
An active site was lost: the Parsa mine contract (Adani Power) has been suspended since September 1, 2023.

Execution risk on capex object: Rs 167 cr of the fresh issue is for commercial vehicles/plant & machinery for which 100% of orders are not yet placed, and deployment has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
Structural end-market risk: thermal (non-coking) coal for power generation is the end-use for most output, exposing volumes to the renewable-energy transition.
Family-controlled: Promoters hold 88.75% pre-Offer and all four executive directors are from the Chadda family.
data_gaps: Offer price band, post-Offer promoter holding %, dilution % and exact OFS share counts are shown as [bullet] in the DRHP; the total Offer of Rs 450 cr comprises a fresh issue of Rs 400 cr and an OFS of Rs 50 cr (Rs 12.50 cr per each of four Promoter sellers).

Industry market size, CAGR and Caliber's market share/positioning were not captured (CRISIL-report figures absent from the routed text), and no market-position basis is stated.

Leverage and DSCR trajectory after the Rs 208 cr debt repayment from Net Proceeds, and the contingent-liability (bank-guarantee) balance versus net worth.
Diesel cost pass-through under fixed-rate contracts and the resulting EBITDA-margin stability.
Trade-receivable days (42/47/52 across FY26/FY25/FY24) and collections from the Coal India subsidiaries.
Placement of orders for the Rs 167 cr capex and FY27 deployment against schedule.
Outcome of the Section 132 search assessments and the AY2025-26 income-tax scrutiny.
Related-party revenue share (16.35% of FY26) and guarantee exposure post-listing.
Expansion progress into new geographies (Odisha, Jharkhand) where no tender application is yet outstanding.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue CAGR 32.67% FY24-FY26 (Rs 953.12 -> 1,677.66 cr); PAT Rs 157.90 cr FY26; order book Rs 9,550.89 cr (~5.7x FY26 revenue) as of May 15, 2026.
RoNW 24.38% and ROE 27.78% FY26, above all four listed peers; but PAT margin ~9.41% and RoNW has declined from 32.41% (FY24) as leverage and scale rose.

CFO Rs 411.04 cr FY26 (positive every year), but capital-hungry: investing outflow Rs 691.92 cr FY26 and net cash decreased in FY24/FY25; cash-flow basis alternates Consolidated/Standalone across years.
Total debt Rs 1,057.61 cr, D/E 1.63x, DSCR 1.12x, net worth Rs 647.54 cr; contingent liabilities 70.81% of net worth and promoter personal guarantees back Rs 1,486.19 cr of borrowings.
Top 3 customers 90.11% of FY26 revenue, no mine ownership, 2-3 year contract-renewal dependence, Parsa site suspended, and ~16.35% of revenue is to related parties.

Income-tax search under Sec 132; RoC penalties for CS non-appointment and a Sec 42 private-placement breach; statutory-dues defaults of Rs 7.44 cr; subsidiaries acquired from Promoters at face value with no independent valuation - partly offset by sector-experienced independent directors.

Total Offer Rs 450 cr = fresh issue Rs 400 cr (repays Rs 208 cr debt + Rs 167 cr capex, benefitting the Company) plus Rs 50 cr promoter OFS; price band is [bullet] so P/E is undetermined, though the June 2026 pre-IPO price of Rs 424 implies ~14.4x FY26 EPS of Rs 29.47.

red_flags: Income-tax search under Section 132 of the IT Act conducted on November 1, 2023 at Company and Promoter premises, with books/documents seized; multiple assessment notices (AY2018-19 to AY2023-24), rectification demands paid under Sec 154, and a fresh Sec 143(2) scrutiny notice for AY2025-26 (June 19, 2026) - proceedings ongoing with undeterminable exposure.

RoC penalties (paid) for two governance lapses: failure to appoint a Company Secretary from December 8, 2022 to July 29, 2024 (Sec 203), and a Section 42 breach where the September 2024 private-placement proceeds of ~Rs 50 cr (Abakkus) were used before PAS-3 filing without a separate bank account.
Delayed statutory dues: total default of Rs 7.44 cr across Provident Fund, TDS, TCS and Professional Tax (PT delays of 104-439 days in FY2024).
Two outstanding criminal proceedings against Promoters relating to fatal motor accidents (Manish Chadda, FIR dated June 4, 2024; Mohit Chadda, as KSR Freight Carrier proprietor).
Subsidiaries Caliber Natural Resources and Caliber Mines and Minerals (99.99% each) were acquired from Promoters at face value with no independent valuation report.
Sharp monetisation gap: Promoter average cost of acquisition is ~Rs 0.60-0.61/share against a June 2026 pre-IPO price of Rs 424 and a Rs 50 cr promoter Offer for Sale.
Company gave a corporate guarantee of Rs 17.70 cr for related party Shree Chadda Roadlines, and Promoter personal guarantees back Rs 1,486.19 cr of borrowings (as of April 30, 2026).

Three struck-off / CIRP entities linked to directors: CS Coal Mining Private Limited (struck off; directorship of Chairman & MD Mohit Chadda), Visionary Legal and Financial Services (struck off; Independent Director Rajendra Prasad Shukla), and India Power Corporation Limited (under CIRP; Independent Director Anil Kumar Jha).
strengths_observed: High-growth, profitable contract miner: revenue from operations grew at a 32.67% CAGR from Rs 953.12 cr (FY24) to Rs 1,430.40 cr (FY25) to Rs 1,677.66 cr (FY26); PAT rose from Rs 95.90 cr to Rs 131.55 cr to Rs 157.90 cr; EPS from Rs 18.80 to Rs 24.55 to Rs 29.47.

Sector-leading return ratios: RoNW 24.38% and ROE 27.78% in FY26 (RoNW 26.89% FY25, 32.41% FY24) - above the RoNW of all four DRHP-named listed peers (Dilip Buildcon 20.09%, Power Mech 15.90%, NCC 9.02%, Sindhu Trade 2.54%).

Large, rising order book gives multi-year visibility: Rs 5,668.30 cr as at March 31, 2026 climbing to Rs 9,550.89 cr as of May 15, 2026 (~5.7x FY26 revenue), of which coal mining services are Rs 5,286.92 cr (93.27%).
Strong operating cash generation: CFO of Rs 411.04 cr in FY26 (Rs 278.37 cr FY25, Rs 48.22 cr FY24), positive in every reported year.
Sovereign-backed anchor customers: primary counterparties are Coal India subsidiaries Western Coalfields (40.95% of FY26 revenue) and Northern Coalfields (44.16%), limiting counterparty credit risk.

Owned, integrated fleet of 1,911 vehicles/plant & machinery (100 leased) with in-house maintenance at seven mining-site workshops, direct month-ahead diesel procurement, and ERP across operations - supporting cost and scheduling control.

Independent directors with direct sector pedigree: ex-Chairman of Coal India (Anil Kumar Jha) and ex-Director (Finance) of Western Coalfields (Rajendra Prasad Shukla), on an 8-member board with 4 independents.
Marquee pre-IPO investors validated pricing at Rs 424/share in June 2026 (Anchorage Capital, Baring PE India, alongside Abakkus at Rs 240 in 2024); no pledge on the Minimum Promoters' Contribution.

Coal is the backbone of India's energy supply, accounting for ~56% of India's primary energy mix and ~75% of total power generation, and is a key raw material for power, steel, sponge iron, cement, paper and brick-kiln industries.
